title: Renewal of Re-Entry Permits for Retired Singapore PRs
what_it_is: Renewal of Re-Entry Permits for Retired Singapore PRs

sections.label: Renewal of retired PRs' REPs
sections.summary: REP renewal depends on criteria including gainful employment, contributions and family roots, with retired PRs generally renewed; about 2% of 52,400 retired applicants were rejected in five years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: A re-entry permit (REP) may be renewed if the Permanent Resident (PR) meets the prevailing criteria for renewal, including whether he or she is gainfully employed and still contributing to Singapore, and has his or her family roots here.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: For PRs who have retired, we will generally renew their REPs, in recognition of their past contributions to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: In the last five years, approximately 52,400 retired Singapore PRs applied to renew their REPs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Only about 2% were rejected, largely because they were absent from Singapore for a prolonged period and furthermore had no family roots here.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: This rejection rate is similar to that from 2010 to 2014.

sections.label: Renewal criteria for retired PRs
sections.summary: Retired PRs cannot declare employment, but REPs are very likely renewed if they show family roots in Singapore or have not been away for prolonged periods.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As the Senior Parliamentary Secretary acknowledged, they have been here for many years and have contributed to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: We generally renew REPs if they are able to show family roots in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The second is that they have not been away from Singapore for prolonged periods of time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: So, like the Member had mentioned, if they are retired PRs, I would understand that they are not able to do a declaration of employment because they are already retired.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: But if they are able to meet the criterion that I just mentioned – that they have family roots or they have not been away for prolonged periods – then, they are very likely to have their REPs renewed.
